Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images Heat and drought have affected shipping, power plants and tourism across eastern Europe – as well as unearthing some surprises By Deborah Cole in Berlin and agencies Sat 1 Aug 2026 07.00 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google B aking temperatures and drought across large swathes of central and eastern Europe have driven water levels on the Danube and Rhine rivers to record lows in some areas, hitting shipping, energy production and tourism hard. View image in fullscreen Extreme conditions aggravated by the climate emergency left Europe’s waterways from the Netherlands to the Black Sea parched, triggering compounding crises. For the first time in their history, Hungary and Romania had to shut down atomic reactors normally cooled by the Danube. The largest nuclear power plant in Hungary, the 44-year-old Paks which supplies nearly half of the country’s electricity, has been cutting output since Monday. View image in fullscreen View image in fullscreen The Paks power plant’s cold-water intake channel from the Danube. The prime minister, Péter Magyar, said the Paks plant was operating at less than ​50% capacity and was expected ​to be ​completely powered down next week. The shutdown could extend for weeks as Danube water ⁠levels are expected to remain too ⁠low to ​restart ‌it. “An energy crisis situation could arise beginning Monday,” he posted on X. “Coordinated steps and restraint will be needed to avoid more severe consequences. We are counting on everyone!” Map of the Danube running across eastern Europe with two nuclear power plants detailed A malfunction at Hungary’s largest gas-fired power plant in Százhalombatta was worsening the grid shortage, he said. Hungarian authorities have asked citizens to reduce energy use in the peak evening hours, including refraining from charging EVs and switching off air conditioners, while carmakers and battery manufacturers have been ordered to cut power and water consumption. In Romania, authorities shut down a reactor unit at the Cernavodǎ power plant earlier in the week for safety reasons and announced a second would be switched off soon after. The prime minister, Ilie Bolojan, said the shutdowns could last for one to two weeks and also urged Romanians to reduce power consumption in the evenings. View image in fullscreen People swimming near a sunken German warship in Prahovo, Serbia . The Danube, which flows through 10 countries, has receded to unprecedented lows in some areas, exposing rocks, old shipwrecks, a second world war bomb and even the remains of an ancient woolly mammoth. A resident of Ryahovo village in northern Bulgaria discovered the bones of the giant ice age beast on the riverbed and specialists at the Regional History Museum in the nearby ‌town of Ruse arrived to investigate the rare find. View image in fullscreen View image in fullscreen View image in fullscreen View image in fullscreen Scientists examining the remains of an ancient mammoth on the dried-up riverbed. Last week, authorities in Budapest closed the Margaret Bridge after a wartime bomb was exposed at its base by the dropping water levels. The record low level of the Danube has forced Budapest cruise ships to dock upriver and sightseeing cruises to be cancelled. Cargo ship operations have ground to a near halt, according to Hungary’s ministry of transport and investment. View image in fullscreen Cattle sit on sand dunes visible after the Danube’s level fell substantially, near Calarasi, Romania. The river is expected to further ebb in the coming days, with no significant rain in the forecast and temperatures expected to exceed 38C across the region. From Slovakia and Hungary to Romania and Bulgaria farther east, ships on the Danube were unable to travel fully loaded along the waterway, and faced lengthy waits. At the Vidin-Calafat Bridge connecting Bulgaria and Romania, Bulgarians said they were out of work because the low water levels had trapped their boats onshore. View image in fullscreen View image in fullscreen A fisher tries to move his boat, blocked by algae on the bottom of the Danube, in front of the Calafat-Vidin Bridge. “It’s never dried up this much before,” Rossen Dobrev, a fisher, told Agence France-Presse. “Now we can even walk all the way to Romania.” Water levels on the Rhine in Germany also fell to near record lows on ⁠Friday, triggered by a heatwave and prolonged dry weather, the country’s WSV navigation agency said. Shallow water has forced reductions of cargo on ‌vessels to about 20% of their normal capacity. View image in fullscreen Three former vessels, including a sailing ship and an eel-fishing boat, connected by a bridge and now serving as a cafe at the old confluence of the Wupper and the Rhine. The Rhine is a crucial shipping artery ​for grains, minerals, ores, coal and oil products, including petrol, creating potential bottlenecks for companies in the EU’s top economy. Dutch officials said the Rhine had dropped to its lowest recorded level at the point where it flows into the Netherlands, and was due to recede further. The Netherlands has suffered from an officially recognised water shortage since mid-July, leading to use restrictions across most of the country, particularly in farming. In Serbia, hundreds of small boats and dozens of cargo ships were marooned on the dried-out riverbank near the northern city of Novi Sad. One houseboat owner, Radovan Segrt, who runs river excursions on his vessel, told the Associated Press that the water in the Danube had withdrawn about 15 to 20 metres from its shore. “The summer season is over now, as far as boat riding is concerned,” he said. Home Paid news feed Foto Agerpres Press Monitoring Bucharest Phone: +4 021.2076.110 Ambassadors, Ukrainian community members mark Ukraine's Independence Day in Bucharest Category: English Date: 2026-08-24 22:56:36 Foto: Grigore POPESCU / AGERPRES Photo Ambassadors and members of the Ukrainian community in Romania celebrated Ukraine's Independence Day in Bucharest on Monday with dances, a photo exhibition, traditional songs and speeches highlighting the resilience of the neighboring people and their desire for peace. 'This anniversary holds special significance. For the fifth consecutive year, we are marking Ukraine's National Day and gathering in this square near the Embassy of Ukraine amid the brutal war of aggression unleashed and waged by the Russian Federation: 1,643 days of full-scale war, the largest war in Europe since World War II. Ukrainian villages, residential areas, energy facilities and other types of civilian infrastructure are being destroyed by daily attacks. Civilians are constantly attacked, targeted and terrorized, with thousands killed or injured,' Ukrainian ambassador in Bucharest Ihor Prokopchuk said. He said Ukraine's spirit of resilience is 'extraordinary' and recalled Ukraine's aspiration to join the European Union, as well as his country's contribution to the security of the EU and NATO space. 'We are confident in the collective strength of Ukraine and its partners who stand by it, on the right side of history,' Prokopchuk said. The ambassador thanked the Romanian Government, Parliament, business community and civil society for standing with Ukraine. Prokopchuk said that since the beginning of the war, approximately five million Ukrainians have been granted temporary protection status in the European Union. Of these, around 200,000 Ukrainians have received such status in Romania. The diplomat explained that this does not necessarily mean that they have to remain in Romania. 'Some have returned [to Ukraine], others have gone elsewhere, but this is where they received temporary protection status,' the ambassador said. Secretary of State with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Ana Tinca paid tribute to the Ukrainians living under wartime conditions. 'On such occasions, we usually recall history and pay tribute to the heroes who built a nation in the past. But today, first and foremost, we are thinking of Ukraine's contemporary heroes, who are many: the soldiers defending the front line with unprecedented courage, the doctors saving lives in the midst of the conflict, the teachers keeping schools open and the parents sending their children to school even though they know they will spend their lessons in shelters, all the ordinary people in Ukraine who keep the country functioning under missile attacks,' she said. The Foreign Ministry official also mentioned those who have had to leave their homes to escape the war, whether elsewhere within Ukraine or abroad. 'They refuse to be victims, they continue to support the struggle for independence and they continue to keep the spirit of Ukraine alive,' she said. Tinca said that the history being created by these people is one 'of courage, dignity and solidarity.' 'Ukraine is not fighting alone. Ukraine is supported by an impressive global network of friends, people and nations, and Romania is proud to be among them. Romania has stood by Ukraine since the first day of the war, and we will continue to support Ukraine until victory and until a just and lasting peace is achieved,' the Secretary of State concluded. https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/s.text: Give Peace A Chance by John Lennon, used in the campaign for tightening Switzerland’s neutrality rules. Photograph: Jean-Christophe Bott/EPA View image in fullscreen Give Peace A Chance by John Lennon, used in the campaign for tightening Switzerland’s neutrality rules. Photograph: Jean-Christophe Bott/EPA Switzerland Swiss voters reject stricter neutrality rules that would have curbed Nato cooperation 70% vote against tightening centuries-old neutrality, which far right said was being eroded by sanctions against Russia Jennifer Rankin Sun 27 Sep 2026 11.05 EDT Last modified on Sun 27 Sep 2026 12.12 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Swiss voters have decisively rejected a proposal for a strict definition of neutrality that would have required Switzerland to curb cooperation with Nato and abandon sanctions against Russia. All cantons and about 70% of voters rejected the proposal for a strictly defined version of neutrality to be ⁠written into the Swiss constitution, final results from the Federal Statistical Office showed. The motion had been promoted by the far-right Swiss People’s party (SVP). Although the defeat was expected, it will be a relief across Europe, amid increasing strains in maintaining EU unity on sanctions against Russia. Switzerland’s centuries-old neutrality was formally recognised after the end of the Napoleonic wars in 1815. Critics of current government policy claim that status has been eroded by Switzerland’s decision to mirror EU sanctions against Russia, after the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Voters were asked to decide on enshrining the principle of “perpetual and armed neutrality” in the constitution and barring Switzerland from joining any military alliances or imposing sanctions on warring states, unless mandated by the UN. The outcome is a heavy defeat for the SVP’s billionaire backer, Christoph Blocher, who was a prominent supporter of the initiative, reported by Bloomberg to have spent 2m francs (€2.1m, £1.8m) on the campaign. Opponents welcomed the results. “Voters understood what the SVP wanted: it wanted Switzerland to isolate itself internationally and shirk its responsibilities when international law is being trampled on,” said Sibel Arslan, a lawmaker for the Green party. The Swiss government, along with most political parties, opposed the measure, arguing “Switzerland would cease to be a reliable partner in international security policy”, leaving the country less secure in the event of an attack and heavily restricting its ability to cooperate with Nato . Although not a member of Nato, Switzerland has cooperated with the transatlantic military alliance for 30 years. Analysts said the result showed Swiss people were content with how the government interpreted Swiss neutrality. “The people have spoken: they accept that neutrality is an instrument that can evolve, leaving the government with room for manoeuvre to adapt its application faced with geopolitical upheavals ,” wrote Katy Romy, a correspondent for SwissInfo, the online service of the Swiss Broadcasting Corporation. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to This is Europe The most pressing stories and debates for Europeans – from identity to economics to the environment after newsletter promotion She also wrote that the yes campaign was unable to shed perceptions it was acting in Russian interests. Russia’s foreign ministry had praised the initiative, while criticising Switzerland’s adoption of EU sanctions and claiming the country was abandoning neutrality. The SVP accepted the defeat and said it had no current plans for further action. https://telex.hu/szepkilatas/2026/10/24/.text: Menü Kereső Ránk számíthattok! 3000 új támogatót keresünk Csatlakozom Hogy került a Stonehenge egy balatoni bazaltkúpra? Szépkilátás Bazaltkapu a Halápon – Fotó: Tenczer Gábor / Telex Tenczer Gábor Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom A Haláp messzebb van a Balatontól az olyan sláger-tanúhegyeknél, mint a Badacsony, a Szent György-hegy vagy akár a Csobánc, ezért sokan nem is ismerik. Leharapott teteje miatt nálunk is a radar alatt volt sokáig, de legutóbb addig nézegettük fura formáját a Kisfaludy-kilátóból, amíg kedvet nem kaptunk hozzá. A Haláp nincs bekötve a turista-úthálózatba, ezért legegyszerűbb elgurulni a déli oldalában fekvő parkolóig és onnan indítani az egyórás sétát. Így rögtön 270 méteres magasságban kezdünk, nagy kaptatásra már nem kell számítanunk. Ha nincs autó, Tapolcáról 5-6 perc alatt odaér a sárga busz Zalahalápra, onnan fél óra gyaloglás a startpont. A parkolóból jobb híján egy salakos-köves úton indulunk el, ami a hegytetőt uraló hatalmas bányaudvar közeli bejáratához vezet. Öt perc se telik bele, máris látjuk, hogy ez a tanúhegy sokkal másabb lesz, mint a többi. Egy hatalmas kőteknő szélén állunk, körben mesterséges kalderaként a karéjban megmaradt határoló bányafal meredezik. A gigászi bazaltlavór két ellentétes oldalán kúpok emelkednek: ezek maradtak mutatóba az egykori hegy magasságából. A bányaudvar és bazaltfala – Fotó: Tenczer Gábor / Telex A három focipályányi sík bányaudvar közepén fura, háromszög alakú faépületek állnak, de egyelőre kihagyjuk őket, mert vonz a magasabb bazaltkúp, aminek emeleti teraszán mágikus törzsi kőszobrokat pillantunk meg. Huhh, ezeket meg kell nézni! Közelebb érve feltűnik, hogy a bányakrátert körben határoló fal egészen különleges „téglákból” áll: a hatszögletű bazaltszálak lecsapott végei úgy lesnek kifelé ezer szemként, mint kettétört óriás spagettik fazékba helyezés előtt. Láttam már badacsonyi bazaltorgonát, bazaltvízesést Somoskőnél, de ezek a szelvények teljesen más dimenzióját mutatják a kőzetnek. A bányafal emeleti teraszára egy köves út visz fel. A terasz szélén körben állnak az indián totemoszlopok és a Stonehenge bumfordi kőszálainak szerelemgyerekei, az Ébredő vulkán néven futó szoborcsoport tagjai. A nyolc, egyenként 3–6 tonnás, nyers vulkáni kőből faragott, ősi és elvont formavilágú alkotást 2019-ben készítette két szobrász: Rhea Marmentini és Balanyi Zoltán. A művészek szándéka az volt, hogy némi gyógyírt helyeznek az egykori bazaltbánya tájsebére, hogy közben emléket állítanak a hegy vulkanikus múltjának is. Hogy ez művészi szándék sikerült-e, csak egy műelemző tudná megmondani, viszont az egészen biztos, hogy a bazaltmonstrumok a bődületes balatoni panorámával a háttérben minden látogatót lenyűgöznek. Köztük minket is. Mini Stonehengbe ojtott totemoszlop-kiállítás – Fotó: Tenczer Gábor / Telex A teraszról egy szűk, meredek, de rövid lépcsősor visz fel a kis megmaradt bazaltkúpra, ami a Haláp 358 méter magas csúcsát képezi. A lépcsősor elején kis tábla lifeg a mentők segélyhívószámával, ha valaki esetleg elszédülne a látványtól. A korláttal lekerített kis csúcsplatóról ugyanis tényleg szédületes panoráma nyílik akár a Balaton, akár a keletre eső bakonyi hegyek fele. Gondos kezek egy ingyenes köztávcsövet is applikáltak a csúcsra, amin hosszan el lehet nézegetni a Tapolcai-medence körpanorámájának részleteit. Idézve a lelkes hangulatú információs táblát: a Halápról elénk táruló táj látványa, bármelyik égtáj fele nézünk, egészen egyedi, megismételhetetlen és csodálatos. Dél felé tekintve a távolban csillogó Balaton víztükre és a többmillió éves vulkanizmusról mesélő tanúhegyek: a Csobánc, jobbról a Tóti, a Gulács, a Badacsony és a Szent György-hegy, északkeletre pedig a Déli-Bakony legmagasabb pontja, az Agár-tető. Lefelé menet rögtön egy keleti terasz fogad panorámapaddal. Muszáj egy kicsit elüldögélni itt is, elbambulva a közeli Hegyesd bimbószerű kiemelkedésén. Úgy döntünk, hogy körbejárjuk a bányakráter peremét az óramutató járásával ellentétes irányban. Csak a tanösvényt kell követni, de érdemes kinézni a külső-belső leágazásaira, mert jó kilátást kínálnak a bányaudvarra és a csúcskúpra, valamint a külső oldalra is. A Haláp csúcsán – Fotó: Tenczer Gábor / Telex A csúcskúppal átellenes északi oldalon az ösvény lejjebb ereszkedik, a törmeléklejtős-erdős hegyoldalra. Itt láthatjuk, milyen lett volna a Haláp, ha nem harapdálják meg a tetejét a bányagépekkel. Páfrányos-mohás, árnyékos, sziklás erdőben lépkedünk kislevelű hársak és bükkök között, a talajszinten hunyor hunyorog. Itt már némi madárfütty is felcsendül, és érthetővé válik, miért is lett a hegy neve Haláp, aminek jelentése eredetileg vizenyős rétre, vadvizes élőhelyre utal. Lassan visszaérünk a parkoló fölé ahonnan indultunk. Ahelyett, hogy lemennénk oda, befelé törekszünk egy úton a bányaudvar közepére. Ott ugyanis vár még minket pár fura faépítmény, ami egy 2023-as építésztábor maradványa. Három évvel ezelőtt ugyanis a Hello Wood építészcsapat installációkat helyezett itt el : az alakjukkal tábortüzet idéző faszerkezetek szándék szerint az újjáéledő hegy szívét jelképezték. A tábort két fesztivál is követte, mára azonban ennek vége, csak a néhány lepattogzó festésű „lángoló piramis” maradt meg. Pihenőnek, bivakszállásnak még egy darabig jók lesznek. A kirándulók így is szeretik, használják még őket. Innen már tényleg a parkoló következik. A túrán három kilométert sétáltunk bő egy óra alatt. A Haláp lenyűgözött minket, egy egészen eredeti hely. Tökéletes levezető túra egy nagyobb tanúhegy kör után, de jó úticél egy Balaton-parti nyaralás feldobására – akár gyerekekkel-családdal is –, egy őszi szüreti átmozgató testmozgásra pedig egyenesen ideális. A bányaudvar és az eredeti formájában megmaradt hegyoldal a kráter külső oldalán – Fotó: Tenczer Gábor / Telex Kis történelem: A Haláp-hegy a legfiatalabb a Balaton-felvidék tanúhegyei közt, potom hárommillió éves. Sokáig büszkén álldogált, majd 1912-ben elkezdték bányászni róla a bazaltot, az ötvenes években pedig rákapcsoltak nagyipari technológiával.
